simple.meaning: טָחָה (ṭâchâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to stretch a bow, as an archer.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Genesis, beginning at Genesis 21:16. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to טָחָה (H2909) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: טָחָה (ṭâchâh) / H2909 is traced through Genesis 21:16 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to stretch a bow, as an archer
definitions.full: H2909. tachah [ טָחָה ] verb hurl, shoot (Late Hebrew id. ; Arabic spread, extend, carry far with , e.g. a ball Lane 1832c ) — only Pil. Participle (Ges § 75 R 18) plural construct קֶשֶׁת כִּמְטַחֲוֵי הַרְחֵק Gen 21:16 (E), literally making distant like shooters of a bow = about a bowshot off.

occurrences.englishText: She went and sat down opposite him, a good way off, about a bow shot away. For she said, “Don’t let me see the death of the child.” She sat opposite him, and lifted up her voice, and wept.
